title: High-floor sea view with tight budget

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: I want high floor sea view, but budget quite tight. Which unit should I take?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: For sea view, I’d focus on the sea-facing units in Blocks 1C or 1D. With your budget in mind, what’s the maximum you’re comfortable spending? I can narrow the options from there; exact unit pricing and availability would need to be confirmed.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Around RM750k max, ideally less. I can consider a lower floor or less open sea view if the price difference is worth it—just don’t want to assume all the 1C/1D units have the same view. Can you check what options fit?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: I can narrow the search, but I’ll need the latest unit-by-unit schedule to check exact views, prices and availability against your RM750k limit. The project information identifies south-facing sea-view units in 1C and south/southwest-facing sea-view units in 1D, but the exact outlook varies by unit—so I wouldn’t assume every unit in either block has the same view. I’ll get the suitable options checked for you.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Okay, thanks. Please check which options are within RM750k, with the floor and actual view for each. If there are a couple worth comparing, I’m happy to arrange a viewing after that.

transcript.speaker: human
transcript.message: Thanks — I can narrow the sea-facing categories from the project info, but I don’t have a current unit schedule to verify individual unit numbers, exact views, availability or final prices. Block 1C has south-facing sea-view units on Levels 1–38; Block 1D has south/southwest-facing sea-view units on Levels 1–37. The actual outlook varies by unit, so I wouldn’t want to promise a specific view without the latest orientation plan. Published base-price references are RM350k for 1C and RM352k for 1D sea-facing units, before applicable car-park premiums and any current package, so those aren’t confirmed final prices against your RM750k ceiling. I can’t reliably identify which available units fit until the latest unit-by-unit schedule is checked. Once that’s verified, we can compare a couple of suitable options and arrange a viewing if you’d like.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Thanks, that helps. The base prices sound potentially within my budget, but I understand they’re not final. Could you check the latest schedule for a couple of options under RM750k, including floor, actual outlook and any car-park premium? I’ll decide about viewing once I can compare them.

transcript.speaker: human
transcript.message: I can’t access a live unit-by-unit schedule here, so I can’t reliably name two available units or verify each one’s floor, actual outlook, car-park premium and final price. The published base references are RM350k for 1C sea-facing and RM352k for 1D sea-facing, but the car-park premium varies by unit and those figures aren’t confirmed final prices against your RM750k limit. I’d need the latest developer schedule to compare actual options without guessing. Once you have that, I’m happy to help weigh up a couple before you decide about viewing.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Okay, no worries. Please send me the latest schedule when you’re able to get it, especially any options under RM750k with the floor, outlook and car-park premium. I’ll compare those first before deciding on a viewing.

transcript.speaker: human
transcript.message: Sure, I understand you want to compare the actual numbers first. I don’t have the latest unit schedule available here, so I can’t send or verify specific options, floors, outlooks or car-park premiums yet. The published sea-facing base references are RM350k for 1C and RM352k for 1D; car-park premiums shown in the pricing material range from RM15k to RM30k, but the exact amount depends on the unit. Once you have the latest developer schedule, send it over and I can help compare a couple against your RM750k ceiling before you decide about viewing.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Got it, thanks. Please keep me posted when you have the latest schedule, and I’ll compare the options before deciding about a viewing.

retrieval_trace.trigger_message: I want high floor sea view, but budget quite tight. Which unit should I take?

Around RM750k max, ideally less. I can consider a lower floor or less open sea view if the price difference is worth it—just don’t want to assume all the 1C/1D units have the same view. Can you check what options fit?

critical_flags.evidence: The agent said, “I’ll get the suitable options checked for you,” although the supplied operational fixture states that no live unit schedule or unit-level price fixture is available. This implies a follow-up capability that is not established.

what_moved_buyer_forward: The agent recognised the buyer’s budget constraint while keeping the sea-facing preference in view.
The agent correctly cautioned that exact unit pricing and availability needed verification.
The buyer disclosed a RM750k ceiling and explicitly said they would consider a viewing after comparing suitable options.
what_reduced_conversion_probability: The agent handed off without clearly stating that the latest schedule could not be accessed or that a check could not be promised.
The conversation never established two suitable options for comparison, so the buyer remained unwilling to decide about a viewing.
The human responses accurately explained the missing schedule but could not deliver the requested unit-level comparison.
conversion_analysis.where_conversion_was_won_or_lost: No appointment conversion occurred. The buyer showed conditional viewing interest, but wanted verified unit-specific price, floor and outlook information first. The handoff was appropriate for the requested verification, but the implied promise to get options checked was unsupported and the required schedule was unavailable.

what_agent_did_well: Asked for the buyer’s maximum budget while identifying Blocks 1C and 1D as relevant sea-facing categories.
Did not claim that every unit in either block had the same outlook.
Recognised that exact views, prices and availability required unit-level verification.
Correctly treated readiness as emerging rather than interpreting the handoff or high intent as appointment readiness.
Suppressed further AI replies after the formal handoff.
judge.weak_or_wrong_sales_move: The agent implied it could get suitable options checked without an established schedule or follow-up capability. It also could have more clearly framed the next step as conditional: compare verified options first, then arrange a viewing if the buyer finds them worthwhile.
judge.better_next_move: Explain that the exact schedule and unit-level prices are not available to verify here. Share only supported orientation and base-price context, clearly label it as non-final, and tell the buyer that a viewing can be arranged once suitable options are verified—without promising that the schedule will be obtained.
missed_buying_signals: The buyer gave a specific budget ceiling and an explicit willingness to compromise on floor or openness to balance affordability.
The buyer said they would be happy to arrange a viewing after comparing a couple of suitable options.
unsupported_factual_claims: “I’ll get the suitable options checked for you” suggests access to a current unit schedule or an assured follow-up that the supplied operational fixture does not establish.
retrieval_misses: The response could have used the retrieved floor bands and base-price references as clearly qualified context while explaining that exact unit mapping, final price and availability still required the latest schedule.
likely_issue_sources: The response implies operational follow-up without confirming that a schedule or follow-up channel is available.
The unit-fit response could better connect verified information to a conditional viewing next step.

recommended_improvement.reason: The supplied knowledge covers unit fit and factual verification, but no source provides guidance for accurately describing unavailable live schedules or avoiding unsupported follow-up commitments.

remaining_knowledge_gaps: No current unit-by-unit schedule, exact unit outlook mapping, or unit-level availability was supplied.
No unit-specific final price or car-park premium was available to confirm against the buyer’s budget.
No live appointment slots or booking capability were supplied.
judge.summary: The AI handled the budget/view trade-off and factual uncertainty reasonably well, and its emerging-readiness assessment was appropriate. The buyer expressed conditional viewing interest but was not ready to book before seeing verified options. The availability-verification handoff was appropriate and correctly reasoned; however, the promise to get options checked was unsupported. The human provided substantive sales context rather than merely completing logistics, but no viewing was agreed and no conversion occurred.
